name: Tohu
overview: Tohu is a male member of the tribe of Levi, noted in Scripture primarily as the father of Elihu and an ancestor of the prophet Samuel. His role is genealogical, linking significant figures within the Levitical lineage. There are no additional notes or narratives about his life beyond these relationships.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Tohu' appears as a proper name without a specified meaning in Scripture. He is also known by the names 'Nahath,' meaning 'descent' or possibly 'rest,' and 'Toah,' both proper names found in related genealogical passages. These variant names reflect the biblical record's transmission of Levitical genealogy but do not carry explicit divine naming significance.
familyAndRelationships: Tohu is explicitly identified as the father of Zuph and Elkanah, and is inferred to be the father of Elihu. Through these sons, he is connected to the lineage leading to Samuel, one of Israel's greatest prophets. Scripture does not provide further family details beyond these recorded relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Tohu's significance lies in his position within the Levitical genealogy, serving as a link in the ancestral line that leads to Samuel. By being the father of Elihu and ancestor of Samuel, he establishes a foundational connection in the biblical narrative that highlights God's providential preservation of His chosen servants. Though not a prominent figure in events, his genealogical role underscores the faithfulness of God's promises through generations.
